purpose: A staged research program for foundational cybersecurity, advanced security engineering, and current standards. Sources guide hypotheses and controls; they are not proof or policy activation.
scope: The existing Crucible pipeline and its project-bound repositories, workflows, custody stores, workers, dashboards, and release paths.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Key Management Guidelines (SP 800-57 family)
observations: Protect key material and metadata against disclosure, substitution, and modification.
Treat generation, storage, distribution, rotation, revocation, backup, and destruction as separate governed lifecycle functions.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: SP 800-63-4 Digital Identity Guidelines
observations: Bind authentication and federation to assurance, lifecycle, session, and privacy requirements.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Secrets Management Cheat Sheet
observations: Centralize storage, provisioning, auditing, rotation, and access control; scope CI/CD identities to only required secrets and services.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions Secure Use Reference
observations: Default GITHUB_TOKEN permissions to read-only, rotate secrets, keep actions current, and avoid granting automation pull-request approval authority.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions OpenID Connect Reference
observations: Use exact repository/ref/audience trust conditions and the minimum id-token permission when replacing long-lived cloud credentials.

authoritativeSourcesReviewed.title: Actions Secrets Reference
observations: Keep secret use within explicit repository or organization scope and do not treat secret names as proof of configured values.

furtherResearch.title: Password managers and protected human intervention
furtherResearch.question: How should Crucible protect operator dashboard and break-glass credentials while supporting password-manager autofill without exposing secrets to the pipeline?

furtherResearch.title: API-key and machine-identity lifecycle management
furtherResearch.question: How should Crucible issue, scope, rotate, revoke, audit and recover machine credentials without putting encryption keys or long-lived tokens into human workflows?

sources.title: RFC 9700 OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice

evidence: NIST SP 800-57 lifecycle separation and protection against substitution/modification
OWASP centralized secret storage, audit, rotation, and scoped CI access
developmentTests: Reject absent or mismatched key fingerprints before decrypt
Verify rotation overlap and revocation without persisting plaintext
Verify recovery metadata cannot substitute ciphertext or key identity

evidence: GitHub Secure Use default read-only token permissions
GitHub OIDC exact subject/audience trust conditions
developmentTests: Reject workflows lacking only the exact permission required
Verify no automation can approve or merge its own pull request

evidence: NIST SP 800-63-4 authentication and federation lifecycle requirements
developmentTests: Reject replayed, expired, wrong-origin, wrong-audience, and missing-state tokens
Verify redacted audit output contains no credential or key value

evidence: GitHub Secure Use guidance on action updates, token permissions, and workflow approval risk
developmentTests: Pin action references and detect dependency drift
Require exact-tip provenance and security checks before retention
